d1e06ee25f72: Create a Bible project · translationCore 4 Help
29fb6289acdc: "You'll add books next. Everything here can be changed later."
64a97739acd7: On Home, click + Add a project, then New Bible (1).
7b22e4876542: New Bible asks How do you want to start? Choose Blank (1), From USFM files (2) or From a Scripture Burrito (3).
636d0009294a: Type a Bible name, for example Kanuri Bible.
3c7c6f2607ec: Type the Language name. When a matching language appears in the list, choose it so Code fills in (for example French (fr) → fr). You can still type the code yourself.
70ec16b2790d: Choose Left to right or Right to left.
10d2318e39dd: Leave Checking language on English. It comes with the app, so you don't need to download anything.
7feed9c56fbe: Click Create Bible →. The Add a book dialog opens. Continue with Add a book.
68c725a1c4f1: Use this when your translation is already in USFM files, one book per file. Each file becomes a book of the new project, with the file's text as its draft.
2a5dd512f36e: Drop your files on Drop your USFM files here, or browse, or click it to choose them. Each file gets a row. A green dot says which book it adds, for example Adds Titus.
1f45b1c1d602: An orange dot means the file can't be used, and the row says why and on which line (1). Remove that file with its ✕, fix it, and add it again.
dad409bd7605: When every row is a book, click Next →.
53baeed24598: Fill in the Bible name, language, code and direction as for a blank Bible. Under the form, Books from your files lists the books (1), and a note says which Versification the books' verse counts fit (2). Most projects keep it.
8e67aa2c4e17: Click Create Bible →. The project is made with all its books in one step, and Add a book opens in case you want more.
d4d9cdd9f9a3: Use this for a Bible translation another tool saved as a Scripture Burrito .zip.
1d065f732497: Click From a Scripture Burrito, then drop the .zip on Drop your Scripture Burrito here, or browse, or click it to choose it.
b2a46e935b31: The form fills in from the Burrito: the name, language and code. Change them if you need to. Books from the Scripture Burrito lists its books (1). A Burrito with its own versification keeps it, and the form says The Scripture Burrito's own versification is kept.
4f7626411f2b: Click Create Bible →. The books and any other files of the Burrito come into the new project, and Add a book opens.
04a7f80fcd39: To cancel at any step, click Cancel, ← Back or the ✕. Nothing is saved.
e47a599c3175: The name needs at least one plain letter or digit, because it also names the project folder. If a project with that name is already on this computer, Create Bible → stays off until you choose another name.
f08e233cb29e: Script font sets the font your translation is shown in. Versification is the verse-numbering scheme; most projects keep the default.
c00ee53c4ea1: If a language code is refused, try the code for your specific language, for example knc for Central Kanuri rather than kau.
36f34cfb4983: Each USFM file must hold one book and start with an \id line. Two files of the same book are refused, and the row names the book.
f694dcfa195d: A Burrito that holds something other than a Bible translation, for example Open Bible Stories, is refused and says what it holds. A Burrito exported from tC4 is work for a project: tC4 asks you to open it with Receive work from a file instead.
e4472267d356: Wait a moment after clicking into a field before you type, then check the name. The first letters can be lost.
f527d4b0c11c: You can change text direction and font later in Project settings. The name and language can't be changed yet.
061c26379bda: The Add a project dialog with five cards: New Bible, marked 1, New Open Bible Stories, Import a project, Open a project from Door43 and Receive work from a file.
90c2e58c6f3f: New Bible, How do you want to start?: Blank, Name the project, then add the books you will translate, marked 1; From USFM files, .usfm, .sfm or .txt · one or many, marked 2; From a Scripture Burrito, .zip · one Bible, marked 3.
edf28ae84c49: The empty New Bible form: Bible name, Language name and Code, Text direction (Left to right selected), Checking language English, recommended and installed with the app, Script font Noto Sans (default), Versification folded away, and Cancel and Create Bible →.
